title: King's Indian Defense: Sämisch Variation
line: A pawn holds White's center, and the kings often castle on opposite wings.

steps.text: The King's Indian, and White pushes the pawn on f2 one square. It guards e4 for good.
Castle first. Your king is safe behind the bishop.
steps.after: White brings out the bishop. The queen comes next, and White may castle on the other side.

steps.text: Strike at the center with the pawn in front of your king.

also.c7c5: That strikes from the side and is the engine's first choice, a pawn gambit. This lesson goes on with the other pawn.

steps.after: White pushes past and the center is closed.

steps.text: Jump the knight to the edge. It clears the way for the pawn on f7.
Now push the pawn on f7 two squares, at White's center.
steps.after: White castles on the queen's side. With the kings on opposite wings, each side can storm the other king.

steps.text: Bring the other knight out, so that the rooks are free to join in.

summary: Against the pawn that holds the center, Black closes it, frees the pawn in front of the rook and attacks the king.
